sentences.text:
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.

This is an application U/S. 482 Cr.P.C. by the petitioner seeking to quash the order taking cognizance of offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n)/376(3)/506 of the IPC r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act.

3. In the course of hearing of this application, Mr. A. Sahoo, learned counsel for the petitioner by filing photocopy of the true copy of depositions of ten witnesses, submits that since a false case has been lodged against the petitioner, the order taking cognizance being unsustainable may kindly be quashed.

On the other hand, Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned AGA submits that when ten witnesses have already been examined in this case, the prayer of the petitioner seems to be infructuous and, therefore, the present CRLMC may kindly be dismissed.

sentences.text: 1 5. A bare perusal of the prayer of the petitioner in this CRLMC would go to disclose that he has challenged the order taking cognizance of offence, but it appears from the submissions and the documents produced by the petitioner that the trial has already commenced and it is at fag end of the case and, therefore, the prayer for quashing of the order taking cognizance offences seems to be infructuous in this situation.
However, the learned counsel for the petitioner also urges this Court to target the disposal of this case.
6. In the result, the present CRLMC stands dismissed on contest, but without any costs.
As requested by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned trial Court may do well to dispose of this case as expeditiously as possible, if there is no other legal impediment.
7. Hence, the present CRLMC stands disposed of.
